processed_hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Abu Waqid al-Laythi: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, while he was sitting in the mosque with people around him, three people approached. Two of them came towards the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and one went away. When they stood at the gathering of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, they greeted. As for one of them, he saw a gap in the circle and sat in it. As for the other, he sat behind them. As for the third, he turned away and left. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished, he said: 'Shall I not inform you about the three people? As for one of them, he sought refuge with Allah, so Allah gave him refuge. As for the other, he was shy, so Allah was shy towards him. As for the other, he turned away, so Allah turned away from him.'

processed_hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Abdullah ibn Abbas: That he spent a night at the house of his maternal aunt Maymunah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ. He said: I lay down across the bed, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his wife lay lengthwise along the bed. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ slept until midnight or a bit before or after it. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ woke up and began to wipe the sleep from his face with his hand. Then he recited the last ten verses of Surah Al-Imran. Then he got up to a hanging water-skin and performed ablution from it, performing ablution well. Then he stood and prayed.

processed_hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Abu Musa al-Ash'ari: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'The likeness of a good companion and a bad companion is like that of the bearer of musk and the blower of bellows. As for the bearer of musk, either he will give you some, or you will buy from him, or you will smell a pleasant fragrance from him. And as for the blower of bellows, either he will burn your clothes, or you will smell an unpleasant odor from him.'
